Hi Eric —

Appreciate the clarity on sizing — that helps. Short answer: yes, we can offer a limited indexation mechanic tied to an agreed GPU cost index. Proposed structure below (high level):

- Term: 24 months, committed GPU-equivalent units (we'll map to reserved SKUs).
- Baseline price: fixed per-token/unit for first 12 months.
- Index trigger: if a published GPU cost benchmark moves >15% (up or down) versus the baseline quarter, pricing can be repriced at a corridor of +/- up to 10% following a review.
- Governance: trigger notification, 10 business day review window, mutual good-faith negotiation; final adjustment requires Finance approval and exec sign-off for changes >5%.
- Protections: caps on upside adjustments for customer (max +10%), floor on downside (min -5% for Redwood).

I've attached a short draft of model mechanics and a sensitivity workbook so you and your CFO can see P&L implications under alternative GPU-price paths. If that looks reasonable I can kick off internal approval.

Next steps: confirm you want indexation on a 24-month commit and whether CloudScale would accept a 15% trigger threshold and the +/-10% corridor.

Best,
Chloe

Team —

I've reviewed the sensitivity workbook. Summary of recommended approval guardrails:

1) Minor repricings (<=5% deviation from baseline): handled by Finance pricing desk — no exec routing.
2) Medium repricings (>5% and <=10%): require CFO sign-off (documented impact analysis).
3) Large repricings (>10%): route to CEO for approval — consider temporary pause of indexation until contract amendment.

Model results (high-level):
- Base case (GPU index +/-5%): net margin impact within acceptable band; no additional discounting needed.
- Adverse market (GPU +25%): under current baseline we would lose ~6-9% margin on the committed run-rate absent greater price pass-through. The proposed corridor limits downside to 10%, which keeps downside loss to ~2-3% after applying our cushion assumptions.

Operational asks for legal and sales: we should specify exact benchmark (e.g., LHR-spot-avg or third-party index) and an audit mechanism. I'll prepare a one-page memo and recommended signature matrix.

Markus
Director, Finance Modeling

Hi Eric / procurement team —

Thanks for the patience while we ran the numbers. We've internally approved the indexation approach with the following agreed points: 

- Trigger threshold: +/-15% vs baseline quarterly GPU index (we propose using the PublicGPUIndex v1 published monthly).
- Corridor: unit price can adjust within +/-10% per trigger, subject to the approval matrix below.
- Approval matrix: <=5% change — Finance pricing desk (no exec); >5% and <=10% — CFO sign-off; >10% — CEO sign-off and contract amendment.
- Implementation: Redwood will send a formal trigger notice within 3 business days of index publication; 10 business day consultation window; final adjustment effective at start of next billing cycle after approvals.
- Protections: customer upside protection (min -5% floor to Redwood); Redwood retains right to pause indexation if capacity becomes materially constrained.
